about: Every model, texture, image and sound in the repository’s asset folders: size, hash, source, licence, the Unreal asset it would become, and what a port does with it.
generatedBy: tools/asset-manifest.mjs; the authored groups are in tools/asset-manifest/groups.mjs

plans.replace: A coherent pack takes its place; the file stands in for scale and intent. `replaceWith` names the pack.
plans.keep: The game’s own; carries over. Import it from the path given.
plans.rework: The content carries over but is re-authored for Unreal.
plans.drop: Only the web build or its tooling needs it.

unrealConventions.import: glTF sources are metres, Y up, right-handed; Unreal’s glTF import converts them (positions ×100, Y and Z exchanged)
unrealConventions.prefixSource: SM_, SK_, T_, M_, MI_, AS_ and DT_ are from Epic’s recommended asset naming conventions; SW_ for sound waves and the texture suffixes are this project’s, as Epic’s page lists none
unrealConventions.naming: Epic’s pattern [AssetTypePrefix]_[AssetName]_[Descriptor]_[OptionalVariantLetterOrNumber], here as [Prefix]_[Family]_[Name] in PascalCase, one asset per name
unrealConventions.lod: The near, middle and far files of one tree or figure are LOD0, LOD1 and LOD2 of one mesh, never three assets. Imported LOD meshes are named <Asset>_LOD0, _LOD1, _LOD2.

trees.brief: Temperate northern European trees with bark, leaf and wind data and three or more LODs: oak, birch, hazel or other shrubs, Scots pine, fir or spruce, apple and pear, and a few palms for the warm woodland in the east.
trees.constraints: The Unreal web target uses the mobile renderer, which has no Nanite, Virtual Shadow Maps or Lumen: choose meshes with real LODs and no Nanite requirement. Epic’s mobile guidance is at most 500,000 triangles and 700 draw calls in view. Megaplants are the exact species but are listed for Unreal Engine 5.7 and 5.8 on Windows only, with Nanite and no LODs, and are edited in the Procedural Vegetation Editor, which Epic marks experimental; the older Megascans Trees are LOD-based.

candidates.title: European Beech
candidates.note: Megascans Trees: 17 meshes with up to nine LODs, impostors and Pivot Painter wind; rated 4.7 by 108. Hornbeam, alder, maple and hazel of the same series were seen in search results, not opened. A northern broadleaf wood without oak or birch.

candidates.title: Megaplants: English Oak
candidates.note: Procedural vegetation: 14 skeletal meshes, Nanite yes, LODs no, Windows only. Silver Birch, Baltic Pine and Norway Spruce of the same series were seen in search results, not opened. The right species for a desktop build; not for the web target.

candidates.title: Apple Tree Pack (Mobile/Desktop)
candidates.note: 17 meshes at 2,000 to 3,000 vertices for mobile and 6,500 to 7,500 for desktop; no LODs; no ratings yet. No pear.

candidates.title: DZ Trees - Low Poly Palms
candidates.note: Made for low-end machines, with LODs; the page says the minimum LODs need adjusting for mobile devices.

rocks.brief: Scanned northern coastal cliffs, beach boulders and rock formations for the strand, the lighthouse rock, the quarry and scattered stones, in a medium or low quality tier.
rocks.constraints: The Unreal web target uses the mobile renderer, which has no Nanite, Virtual Shadow Maps or Lumen: choose meshes with real LODs and no Nanite requirement. Epic’s mobile guidance is at most 500,000 triangles and 700 draw calls in view. These are single scanned Megascans assets, free, delivered as FBX and glTF in quality tiers, not packs: take the Mid or Low tier and gather the set piece by piece.

candidates.title: Nordic Coastal Cliff
candidates.note: One scanned cliff piece, 1.0 × 2.6 × 4.1 m, as FBX and glTF; displacement on the high tier only. Huge and Massive variants were seen in search results, not opened.

candidates.title: Nordic Beach Rock Formation
candidates.note: One scanned formation, 4.2 × 4.2 × 1.3 m, as FBX and glTF. Nordic Beach Boulder and Rock were seen in search results, not opened.

buildings.brief: One modular kit of plain northern European village buildings that can be entered: timber-frame and rubble-stone walls, plaster, plank, thatch or tile roofs, doors, windows and stairs, with interior walls and floors. The mill, the quarry sheds and the watchtower are assembled from it or dressed around it.
buildings.constraints: The Unreal web target uses the mobile renderer, which has no Nanite, Virtual Shadow Maps or Lumen: choose meshes with real LODs and no Nanite requirement. Epic’s mobile guidance is at most 500,000 triangles and 700 draw calls in view. The game’s buildings are placed from data/unreal/DT_Buildings.json by footprint, wall height and roof kind: a kit of fixed whole houses will not fit those footprints, a modular one will.

candidates.title: Medieval Modular Town (With Interiors)
candidates.note: 393 static meshes with collision and LODs (generated, some custom), 31 materials with 122 instances, and explorable interiors; rated 4.7 by 18.

surfaces.appliesTo: The Landscape’s eight ground layers. The web build generates its ground textures in code, so no file in this manifest stands for them.
surfaces.brief: Tiling ground surfaces for the Landscape’s eight layers: forest floor, heath, earth path, gravel, sand and wet sand; and plaster, timber, rubble stone, slate and thatch only if the building kit does not bring its own.
surfaces.constraints: A Landscape material on the mobile renderer is limited in texture samplers: plan the eight layers as few shared texture sets. No scanned surface was found for heath, wet sand or a dirt path.

candidates.title: Forest Floor
candidates.note: A scanned 2 × 2 m surface as a texture set. Mossy Forest Floor was seen in search results, not opened.

candidates.title: Gravel on Soil
candidates.note: A scanned 0.39 × 0.39 m surface as a texture set. Ground Gravel was seen in search results, not opened.

candidates.title: Nordic Beach Rocky Ground
candidates.note: A scanned ground patch, 2.3 × 2.9 m, as FBX and glTF.

interiors.brief: Plain medieval household furniture and props in one material language: beds and bunks, tables, benches, chairs, shelves, chests, a loom, a workbench, barrels, crates, sacks, pots, a cauldron, bread, candles, and an oven and hearth dressing.
interiors.constraints: The Unreal web target uses the mobile renderer, which has no Nanite, Virtual Shadow Maps or Lumen: choose meshes with real LODs and no Nanite requirement. Epic’s mobile guidance is at most 500,000 triangles and 700 draw calls in view. Avoid throne-room and high-fantasy pieces; the look is weathered and poor.

candidates.title: Medieval Banquet
candidates.note: 84 scanned meshes with LODs and no collision: tableware and food more than furniture.

candidates.title: Medieval Props: Kit
candidates.note: 266 unique models in six sets (furniture, kitchen, cellar, books and more) with custom collision and two LODs each, about 3,500 triangles at LOD0. Pick the plain pieces.

candidates.title: Medieval Fantasy Furniture Pack 01
candidates.note: 31 low-poly furniture models with three material variants and four LODs each.

characters.brief: One modular set of grounded medieval villagers on the engine’s standard skeleton, enough to dress seventeen residents (reeve, steward, foreman, workers, baker, hunter, recorder, warden, caravan master, bandits) and a hero, with LODs; or MetaHumans with medieval clothing for a desktop build.
characters.constraints: The Unreal web target uses the mobile renderer, which has no Nanite, Virtual Shadow Maps or Lumen: choose meshes with real LODs and no Nanite requirement. Epic’s mobile guidance is at most 500,000 triangles and 700 draw calls in view. MetaHuman bodies are heavy for the web target. No miller, baker, priest or hero figure was found as such: they come from dressing a modular set.

candidates.title: Modular Medieval Citizens
candidates.note: One modular peasant with 13 body parts, colour masks and face blend shapes, rigged to the Epic skeleton, with two LODs. Listed for engine versions up to 5.0 only; rated 3.5 by 10.

candidates.title: Medieval NPC Pack v1
candidates.note: Five fixed villagers of 4,200 to 5,400 vertices on the Unreal Engine 5 skeleton with 101 in-place animations; no LODs.

candidates.title: Modular Medieval NPC V2 - Metahuman
candidates.note: About 130 modular clothing meshes for men and women on the Unreal Engine 5 skeleton, with MetaHuman integration; no animations; rated 4.3 by 8. By far the dearest candidate.

animation.brief: Animation on the standard skeleton for locomotion, work and idling, sitting and lying down, unarmed and sword combat with guard and dodge, the bow, swimming, and mounting and riding.
animation.constraints: No bow set and no deer-riding set was found; a horse rider set is the nearest. Epic’s Game Animation Sample shows the standard Personal and Professional licences on its page; an earlier report that it is limited to Unreal Engine products was not confirmed there, so read its licence before using it elsewhere.

candidates.title: Game Animation Sample
candidates.note: A complete project with motion-matched locomotion and traversal; rated 4.7 by 358. No combat, swimming, bow or riding.

candidates.title: Sword Animset Pro
candidates.note: 178 motion-captured sword animations on the Unreal Engine 4 template skeleton, in place and with root motion; retarget them to the newer skeleton. Fighting Animset Pro for unarmed combat was seen in search results, not opened.

candidates.title: MC Village Life Animation Pack
candidates.note: Motion-captured village work, idle and sitting motions on the Unreal Engine 5 mannequin skeleton, in place and with root motion; rated 4.5 by 6.

candidates.title: Swim Animset
candidates.note: Freestyle, breaststroke at three speeds, floating idles, turns and diving on the Epic skeleton. Listed up to 5.4 only; rated 3.1 by 7.

animals.brief: Rigged, animated animals with LODs and gaits: deer and stag, wolf, bear, boar, lion and tiger, cat and dog; a saddled deer or a mount that can stand in for it; ideally with their calls.
animals.constraints: The Unreal web target uses the mobile renderer, which has no Nanite, Virtual Shadow Maps or Lumen: choose meshes with real LODs and no Nanite requirement. Epic’s mobile guidance is at most 500,000 triangles and 700 draw calls in view. No standalone realistic animated tiger was found, and no dog pack was opened.

candidates.title: FOREST ANIMALS PACK
candidates.note: Bear, boar, doe, stag, fox, rabbit and wolf at about 5,000 vertices, each in three levels of detail with 8 to 24 animations; rated 4.4 by 41. Listed up to 5.4 only.

candidates.title: ANIMAL VARIETY PACK
candidates.note: A free assortment from the same maker, 1,200 to 5,700 vertices with 17 to 26 animations each; rated 4.7 by 337. Search results named stag, doe, wolf, fox, pig and crow.

candidates.title: African Animals
candidates.note: 21 animals with 1,318 animations, among them a lion with a groomed mane.

candidates.title: Cats Pack
candidates.note: Twelve cats (four builds in several coats) with 175 animations; models and animations only, no controllers.

audio.brief: Sound libraries to fill gaps in the game’s own set: nature ambience beds (forest, coast, wind, stream), footsteps by surface, medieval village and work foley, weapon and bow foley, and restrained medieval music.
audio.constraints: The game’s own clips are balanced against each other; replace single weak clips, not the set. Check that a library’s licence covers game distribution.

candidates.title: Wilderness Nature Loops
candidates.note: 200 seamless nature loops, 349 minutes, 44.1 kHz 16-bit.

candidates.title: Foley: Footsteps Sound Effects Pack
candidates.note: 324 footstep samples on several surfaces, shod and barefoot, meant to be played at random.

candidates.title: Medieval Fantasy Game Music Pack
candidates.note: 32 tracks, an hour of music: 14 full pieces, 14 loops and 4 diegetic pieces.

groups.title: The wanderer (hero body and animation)
groups.why: A generated body on a generated rig, with unresolved provenance for two of its sources. A commercial port needs a character with clear terms: a MetaHuman or a modular medieval character from one pack, on the engine’s standard skeleton so animation packs retarget.
groups.source: Generated with Meshy; see docs/engineering/main-hero.md and the model ledger.

replaceWith.title: Modular Medieval NPC V2 - Metahuman
replaceWith.reason: The only candidate that is modular, dresses men and women, and lists current engine versions (5.0 to 5.8), so one set can make seventeen residents and the hero. It is by far the dearest. Modular Medieval Citizens is cheaper but lists versions up to 5.0 only and is rated 3.5. For the web target, the five low-poly villagers of Medieval NPC Pack v1 are light enough.

groups.title: Residents and hostiles (17 figures)
groups.why: Seventeen separately generated figures of uneven proportion and surface. One modular villager set gives a coherent cast, shared skeleton and LODs.
groups.source: Generated or downloaded Meshy models, adapted; see docs/engineering/meshy-npcs.md and the model ledger.

replaceWith.title: Modular Medieval NPC V2 - Metahuman
replaceWith.reason: The only candidate that is modular, dresses men and women, and lists current engine versions (5.0 to 5.8), so one set can make seventeen residents and the hero. It is by far the dearest. Modular Medieval Citizens is cheaper but lists versions up to 5.0 only and is rated 3.5. For the web target, the five low-poly villagers of Medieval NPC Pack v1 are light enough.

groups.title: Resident rig measurements
groups.why: Per-figure joint and garment measurements for the web build’s own posing. A port’s characters bring their own rigs.

groups.title: Resident motion library
groups.why: Generated clips fitted to the generated rigs. Locomotion, work, sitting and combat should come from an animation pack on the standard skeleton.

replaceWith.title: MC Village Life Animation Pack
replaceWith.reason: Village work, idling and sitting are most of what residents do, and this set is on the current skeleton and lists engine versions up to 5.8. Locomotion, sword combat and swimming come from the three companions; the swim set lists versions up to 5.4 only.

groups.title: Animals (19 rigged models)
groups.why: Community models of mixed quality with in-place clips only. An animal pack supplies matched skeletons, gaits, LODs and often sounds.
groups.source: Meshy Community downloads, optimised and rigged; see docs/engineering/meshy-animal-assets.json.

replaceWith.title: FOREST ANIMALS PACK
replaceWith.reason: It has the deer, wolf, bear, boar and fox of the game’s woods in three levels of detail from one maker. The lion comes from African Animals and the cats from Cats Pack; no tiger and no dog pack was found. It lists engine versions up to 5.4, so migrating it is part of the work.

groups.title: Supplied trees (15 kinds, three levels each)
groups.why: Generated trees with card crowns rebuilt in code. Scanned tree sets bring real bark, leaf and wind data and proper LODs; the planting (data/world/flora.json) carries over.
groups.source: Meshy Community downloads, rebuilt by tools/build-meshy-trees.py; see docs/engineering/meshy-tree-assets.json.

replaceWith.title: Megaplants: English Oak
replaceWith.reason: The exact species of the game’s woods (oak, with birch, pine and spruce in the same series), free. They need Nanite and list 5.7 and 5.8 on Windows only, so the LOD-based Megascans Trees stand in on the web target, with the palm and apple packs for the kinds neither series has.

groups.title: Generated trees (hero oak, birch, apple, pear, bush, sentinel, pine)
groups.why: The project’s own procedural trees (tools/tree-gen), built for the web build’s triangle budget. They are original and may be kept as a fallback, but a port should use one tree source throughout.
groups.source: Generated by tools/tree-gen and tools/tree-gen-pine; project-original.

replaceWith.title: Megaplants: English Oak
replaceWith.reason: The exact species of the game’s woods (oak, with birch, pine and spruce in the same series), free. They need Nanite and list 5.7 and 5.8 on Windows only, so the LOD-based Megascans Trees stand in on the web target, with the palm and apple packs for the kinds neither series has.

groups.title: Solitary pine (three levels)
groups.why: As the supplied trees: replaced with the conifers of the chosen tree set.
groups.source: Meshy Community download, adapted; see docs/engineering/solitary-pine.md.

replaceWith.title: Megaplants: English Oak
replaceWith.reason: The exact species of the game’s woods (oak, with birch, pine and spruce in the same series), free. They need Nanite and list 5.7 and 5.8 on Windows only, so the LOD-based Megascans Trees stand in on the web target, with the palm and apple packs for the kinds neither series has.

groups.title: Scenery models (rock pile, ancient broadleaf)
groups.why: Two one-off generated models. Rocks and landmark trees come from the scanned rock and tree sets.
groups.source: Meshy Community downloads, adapted; see docs/engineering/rock-pile-assets.json and broadleaf-assets.json.

replaceWith.title: Nordic Beach Rock Formation
replaceWith.reason: A free scanned formation of the northern coast the game’s strand is modelled on, with the cliff piece for the lighthouse rock. Both are single assets: more pieces of the same Nordic series are needed for variety.

groups.title: Furniture and household pieces (29 models)
groups.why: Generated pieces at inconsistent texel density. A medieval interior pack gives one material language; sizes and placements (data/world/interiors.json) carry over.
groups.source: Generated with Meshy for the project; see docs/engineering/rooms-0.0.13.md.

replaceWith.title: Medieval Props: Kit
replaceWith.reason: The widest set in one material language: furniture, kitchen and cellar pieces with collision and two LODs each, listed up to 5.8. The furniture pack adds beds and chests with four LODs.

groups.title: Furniture size manifest
groups.why: Measured sizes for the web build’s loader; the sizes the game uses are in the core.

groups.title: Wind test tree
groups.why: A fixture for the web build’s foliage wind tests.

groups.title: Baked building surfaces (12 materials, colour and normal)
groups.why: Procedurally baked plaster, timber, stone and metal for the web build’s merged building geometry. Buildings in a port come as modular kits with their own scanned or authored materials.

replaceWith.title: Medieval Modular Town (With Interiors)
replaceWith.reason: The one modular kit found whose buildings can be entered, with collision and LODs and engine versions up to 5.8. Its timber frame is richer than the game’s poor village: use the plain pieces and its interiors.

groups.title: Building surface manifest
groups.why: Hashes for the web build’s texture loader.

groups.title: Leaf atlases
groups.why: Leaf cards cut for the web build’s crowns from the supplied trees’ textures. Replaced together with the trees.
groups.source: Built by tools/leaf-atlas from the supplied tree textures.

replaceWith.title: Megaplants: English Oak
replaceWith.reason: The exact species of the game’s woods (oak, with birch, pine and spruce in the same series), free. They need Nanite and list 5.7 and 5.8 on Windows only, so the LOD-based Megascans Trees stand in on the web target, with the palm and apple packs for the kinds neither series has.

groups.title: Hegemony emblem
groups.why: The approved faction emblem of the title screen: part of the game’s identity. Import the PNG; the WebP is the web build’s smaller copy.
groups.source: Approved identity artwork from the Warpkeep-Assets repository; see docs/engineering/menu-assets.json.

groups.title: Title music: The Sovereign’s Oath
groups.why: The title theme the menu’s grove is choreographed to. Import the archived original; the OGG and M4A are web encodings. Its service terms are recorded as unresolved and must be cleared before a commercial release.
groups.source: Supplied by the project owner; see docs/engineering/menu-score.md and menu-audio-assets.json.

groups.title: Spoken lines, web sprites (240 sprite files in two encodings)
groups.why: Each speaker’s lines joined end to end for the browser. A port imports the single takes from the source archive.

groups.title: Spoken lines, single takes
groups.why: The game’s own dialogue, one file a line, keyed as data/game/voice.json. Synthetic voices: keep as the working track and decide on recorded actors before release.
groups.source: ElevenLabs text to speech with designed voices; see docs/engineering/voice-assets.json.

groups.title: World sound, web banks and loops
groups.why: Effects packed into banks, and loops and music re-encoded, for the browser. A port imports the source clips.

groups.title: World sound, source clips (effects, ambience beds, music)
groups.why: Foley, ambience and the adaptive score, generated for this world and already balanced against each other. Keep them; where a bed or effect is weak, a sound library from Fab fills the gap.
groups.source: ElevenLabs Sound Effects and Eleven Music; see docs/engineering/world-audio-assets.json.

groups.title: Animal calls, web encodings
groups.why: Browser encodings of the calls in the source archive.

groups.title: Animal calls, source clips
groups.why: Two generated calls per kind, made for these animals. Keep them: no Fab library with the calls of all of them was found. Where the chosen animal pack brings recorded calls for an animal, use those.

groups.title: Hunting sounds (bow, arrow, skinning)
groups.why: Six effects made for the bow and the knife. Keep; a weapon foley library can replace any that read as synthetic.

groups.title: Hunting sound manifest
groups.why: Hashes for the web build’s loader.

groups.title: Warpkeep model archive (209 models)
groups.why: Byte-exact copies of another project’s models, kept for provenance and not built into the game. They are not offered under an open licence and do not go into a port.

groups.title: Warpkeep archive manifest
groups.why: The archive’s own file list.
